LESSON: LISTENING AND SPEAKING 4.1.1 PRONUNCIATION AND VOCABULARY

Grade: Grade 5
Subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE
Strand: Strand 4
Topic 4.1: Listening and Speaking 4.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 3

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Listening and Speaking 4.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary, part of Strand 4 in Grade 5 ENGLISH LANGUAGE.

Key inquiry question: Why should we pronounce words correctly? 2. Why do words have different meanings at times?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. recite a poem featuring the words skid, speed, hit and run, reckless, block, traffic, fatal, rescue, ambulance, road signs,

2. apply the correct stress on the words skid, speed, hit and run, reckless, block, traffic, fatal, rescue, ambulance, road signs,

3. listen/watch to an audio-visual 1.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. recite a poem featuring the words skid, speed, hit and run, reckless, block, traffic, fatal, rescue, ambulance, road signs,
2. apply the correct stress on the words skid, speed, hit and run, reckless, block, traffic, fatal, rescue, ambulance, road signs,
3. listen/watch to an audio-visual 1.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Listening and Speaking 4.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Communication and Collaboration is enhanced as the learner practises correct pronunciation of sounds and words

in small groups.

• Self-efficacy is developed as learners recite poems and stress words correctly.

Values:
Peace is fostered as the learner displays tolerance with peers struggling to distinguish between sounds /t/ and /d/ during

pronunciation and they as help one another to improve their pronunciation.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Safety and security is promoted as the learner interacts with content on accident prevention.

Link to other Learning Areas:

The learner applies the knowledge derived from the theme accident and road safety to the concept of accidents is learnt

in such learning areas as Environmental Studies.
